title: Resume partially delivered streams after retryable socket closure without duplicating output
before: At parent commit 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2, the stream loop could replay a request only when the current attempt had produced no non-thought content. If a retryable socket-level transport error occurred after visible answer text had reached the caller, replay was rejected to avoid duplication and the transport error propagated. Text-only partial output was not durable history, so there was no continuation path that both preserved the caller's visible prefix and reconstructed the complete model turn.
after: At d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5, retryable transport cuts with accumulated nonblank text and no function call enter a separately budgeted continuation path. Each continuation request temporarily appends the delivered model prefix and a fenced resume instruction, emits a continuation RETRY so consumers retain displayed text, deduplicates overlap at attempt boundaries, and merges the delivered prefix into the successful trailing model turn. Fresh-restart retries and reactive compression clear staged continuation state; function-call cuts and exhausted continuation budgets still propagate.
diff: The change adds a three-attempt continuation budget and shared recovery-message construction; tracks per-attempt and accumulated delivered text plus function-call presence; distinguishes clean replay from continuation using accumulated visible output; creates request-only synthetic continuation turns; emits continuation-aware retry events; resets staged state whenever another recovery branch restarts from rebuilt/original contents; folds repeated overlap between attempts; and prepends the recovered prefix into durable history. The test suite adds scenarios for successful continuation, history reconstruction, repeated cuts, overlap removal, thought-only or empty later attempts, budget exhaustion, function-call exclusion, clean replay cases, and continuation supersession by other retry paths.

    * fix(core): resume long streams cut by a socket-level close
    
    Long generations that are cut mid-response by a gateway SSE idle timeout
    (DashScope closes at ~3-5 min) failed outright, however many retries were
    configured. The stream retry loop could only recover by *replaying* the
    request, and that path is gated on `!streamYieldedChunk` — by the time a
    long answer is cut, chunks have obviously been delivered, so the gate was
    shut exactly when recovery was needed.
    
    Two changes:
    
    - Widen the replay gate from "any chunk yielded" to "visible output
      yielded" (non-blank answer text or a functionCall). Thinking models emit
      reasoning within seconds, which made replay unreachable for the very
      generations that need it. The UI's non-continuation RETRY handler clears
      the thought buffer, and the rate-limit and invalid-stream branches
      already re-send after thoughts have streamed, so this matches existing
      behaviour rather than adding risk.
    
    - Add continuation recovery for cuts that already delivered answer text,
      where replaying would duplicate what the caller has on screen. Keep the
      delivered text, ask the model to resume from it, and emit
      `{ RETRY, isContinuation: true }` so the UI keeps its text buffer — the
      same shape the MAX_TOKENS truncation path already uses. The synthetic
      turns are built into the request only, never written to `history`, so
      they cannot leak into the transcript or a later compression; on success
      the delivered prefix is merged back into the trailing model turn, with
      replayed overlap deduped by the existing recovery helper. Budget of 3,
      since one generation can be cut repeatedly by the same timeout.
    
    Cuts that delivered a `functionCall` are excluded: injecting a user turn
    between a `functionCall` and its `functionResponse` yields a sequence
    providers reject, and the scheduler's repair path already covers it.
    
    Fixes #7832
    
    * fix(core): reset continuation state on every fresh-restart retry
    
    Review found that the `suppressNextRetryEvent` arm bypasses the
    continuation reset. Two branches emit a non-continuation RETRY *and* set
    `suppressNextRetryEvent`, so the next loop iteration takes the suppress
    arm and skips the `else if` that clears the staged continuation:
    
    - the transport replay branch, reachable when a continuation attempt is
      itself cut before yielding visible output, and
    - the reactive compression branch, which is if anything more likely on a
      continuation attempt, since that request carries the delivered text and
      the resume instruction on top of the original contents.
    
    Either way the UI has dropped the delivered text (plain RETRY) while the
    request still asks the model to resume from it, and the merge on success
    writes that discarded text back into history — a permanent UI/history
    mismatch visible on `/compress` and `--resume`.
    
    Extract the reset into `resetTransportContinuation()` and call it from
    both branches before they set the flag. Resetting inside the suppress arm
    instead would clear the state of a continuation that is legitimately in
    flight.
    
    The pre-existing supersession test used `InvalidStreamError`, whose retry
    branch does not set `suppressNextRetryEvent`, so it exercised the
    `else if` path and neither trigger. Add a test per branch; both fail if
    their reset is removed.

    raw `+=`. Overlap dedup ran only at merge time, comparing the *final*

    context of every later turn.

    continuation branch, the second case fell into it: `resetTransportContinuation()`

    to discard output the user was watching, after which the model regenerated it

    continues and never replays. The `resetTransportContinuation()` call inside the

## Why

HTTP retries used local backoff even when the server supplied `Retry-After`. Relative retry delays also failed to account for time spent propagating errors or reporting retries.

## What changed

- Parse `Retry-After` delay seconds and HTTP dates into a monotonic deadline captured when response headers arrive.

- Preserve deadlines through API and Bedrock error mapping, stream retries, and exhausted retry state. Expired advice remains a zero delay instead of triggering local backoff.

## Testing

Add coverage for header parsing, deadline countdown and expiry, error mapping after exhausted HTTP retries, and delayed stream retry notifications. Update Responses and remote compaction tests

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit identifies the defect as HTTP retries using local backoff despite Retry-After and relative delays failing to account for propagation or reporting time; it states that the fix parses advice into a monotonic deadline and preserves it through retry paths.

RetryAfter represents the earliest advised follow-up time as a Tokio Instant, parses nonnegative delay seconds or HTTP dates, exposes the original deadline, and saturates expired remaining delay to zero.
Before the change, the HTTP retry loop contained an explicit TODO to respect Retry-After, always computed local backoff, and slept for that relative duration.
The HTTP transport captures Retry-After from response headers before consuming the body and stores the resulting advice on non-success TransportError::Http values.
The HTTP retry loop now uses the captured advice when present, records its remaining delay, and sleeps until its original deadline; local backoff remains the fallback only when advice is absent.

The protocol error representation changed from an optional relative Duration to an optional RetryAfter deadline; remaining server delay is derived at observation time, and expired advice remains Some(Duration::ZERO).

API-to-protocol error mapping extracts retry advice before changing error details and reapplies the same RetryAfter value to the mapped error, including retryable, rate-limit, overload, and HTTP transport errors.
Provider-specific expired-signature remapping preserves the original retry deadline while replacing the user-facing error details.

Response-stream retry handling reads the preserved deadline, performs notification work, recomputes the remaining telemetry delay, sleeps until the original deadline, and stores that deadline when retries are exhausted.
Parser tests verify delay-seconds countdown, HTTP-date handling, explicit zero and expired dates as valid zero-delay advice, and rejection of malformed or overflowing values.
A paused-time stream test delays retry notification and verifies that the retry resumes at the original server deadline rather than waiting the full relative duration after notification completes.
An exhausted-HTTP-retry test verifies that the last captured deadline survives API error mapping, counts down across elapsed time, and remains present with zero remaining delay after expiry.

End-to-end response retry coverage returns a 503 with Retry-After: 1, verifies HTTP-layer retry telemetry, waits at least the advised interval, completes successfully, and observes exactly two requests.
Remote compaction coverage verifies that a 503 carrying Retry-After is retried at the HTTP layer after the advised interval and that compaction completes through the subsequent successful response.
A provider-specific test verifies that rewriting an expired-signature error retains the exact RetryAfter value.
